questions.question: When butane boils, what is actually overcome?
options: The covalent bonds inside each molecule
Both the covalent bonds and the intermolecular forces
The bonds between carbon and hydrogen only

questions.question: The only intermolecular force acting between nonpolar alkane molecules is:
Hydrogen bonding occurs between molecules when hydrogen is bonded directly to:
For equal chain length, the correct ranking of families from weakest to strongest intermolecular forces is:
Boiling points rise from methane to octane because longer chains have:
options: Larger surfaces and more electrons, so stronger London forces

questions.question: Pentane boils at 36,1 °C but its isomer 2,2-dimethylpropane boils at 9,5 °C. The reason is that the branched isomer:
options: Has a compact shape with less surface contact, weakening the dispersion forces

questions.question: Which compound has the HIGHEST boiling point?
As the strength of intermolecular forces increases, boiling point and vapour pressure respectively:
Butane (M = 58 g·mol⁻¹) boils at −0,5 °C while propan-1-ol (M = 60 g·mol⁻¹) boils at 97,2 °C. The main reason is that propan-1-ol:
options: Forms hydrogen bonds between its molecules

questions.question: Propanal boils higher than butane of the same molar mass because aldehydes have:
options: Dipole-dipole forces in addition to London forces

questions.question: Carboxylic acids boil higher than alcohols of similar size because their molecules:
options: Have no London forces to weaken them
Hydrogen-bond at two sites, forming pairs held by a double hydrogen bond

questions.question: Short alcohols dissolve in water while alkanes do not, because alcohols:
options: Have weaker intermolecular forces than water

subtopics.title: Vapour Pressure and the Four-Step Answer

questions.question: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by:
options: The atmosphere on the surface of a liquid
A gas being compressed in a syringe
The vapour of a liquid in equilibrium with the liquid, in a closed container
A boiling liquid on the walls of its container

questions.question: A volatile liquid is one with:
options: Weak intermolecular forces and a high vapour pressure
Strong intermolecular forces and a high vapour pressure

questions.question: A liquid boils when:
options: Its vapour pressure equals the surrounding atmospheric pressure

questions.question: The final step of the four-step explanation for a boiling point difference must link stronger forces to:
options: More energy needed to overcome them

questions.question: In the velcro picture, a longer carbon chain means:
options: A longer strip of velcro — more grip and a higher boiling point

questions.question: Branching lowers the boiling point because a branched molecule is like:
options: A strip of velcro with extra hooks
A crumpled ball of velcro that touches its neighbours only in patches
A magnet that has lost its pull

questions.question: When a liquid boils, what tears apart?
options: The grip between molecules — the molecules stay intact
The hydrogen atoms from the carbons
The functional groups from the chains

questions.question: In the analogy, the "fridge magnets" carried by aldehydes and ketones represent:
options: Dipole-dipole attraction between their polar molecules

questions.question: The strongest grip in the syllabus — the "handshake" — belongs to molecules whose hydrogen is bonded directly to:
options: An oxygen, as in an alcohol's OH group

questions.question: Carboxylic acids top the boiling-point ladder because their molecules:
options: Hold hands in pairs, clasped by two hydrogen bonds

questions.question: Petrol refuses to mix with water because its molecules offer water:
options: Only London forces, which cannot compete with water's hydrogen-bond network

questions.question: Nail polish remover empties itself from an open bottle because its molecules:
options: Grip each other weakly, so many escape — a high vapour pressure

questions.question: Strong intermolecular forces give a liquid:
options: A high vapour pressure and a low boiling point
A high vapour pressure and a high boiling point
A low vapour pressure and a low boiling point
A low vapour pressure and a high boiling point

questions.question: You can smell an ester across a room because esters:
options: Are volatile enough for many molecules to escape into the air
Dissolve in the air's water vapour

questions.question: The four-step explanation for any boiling point or vapour pressure difference runs:
options: Structural difference, forces named, strengths compared, energy linked
